Governance is not a policy document. It is the environment the work happens in.

Governance, built in

Enterprise controls on every workflow

  • Permission scopes. Every agent operates inside least-privilege scopes you define — by role, system and data class.
  • Approval gates. Sensitive actions — refunds, contracts, data deletion — pause for human sign-off, by policy.
  • Audit trail. Every action, decision and handoff is logged immutably and exportable to your SIEM.
  • Cost governance. Per-agent budgets, hard ceilings and alerts keep spend predictable at any scale.
The Governance Layer — our doctrine

Four invariants. One honesty standard.

INVARIANT 01

“Capability ≠ Authority”

“Ability is not authority.” An AI that can do a thing is not an AI that may do a thing — every agent carries least-privilege permissions per role: what it may touch, spend, say or send.

INVARIANT 02

“Execution ≠ Liability”

“Execution is not liability.” Your business stays accountable. Our AI carries work inside delegated scope — and the boundary of that scope is written, enforced and auditable.

INVARIANT 03

“Deployment ≠ Adoption”

“Deployment is not adoption.” Going live proves nothing by itself. We prove outcomes against go-live acceptance criteria you sign — and report against them openly.

INVARIANT 04

“Continuity ≠ Persona”

“Continuity is not persona.” Your memory, rules and evidence belong to your business and stay with it — portable, exportable, never locked to one setup.

Responsibility layers

Who holds authority — and where the boundary sits

1
Principal

You — the authority holder. Nothing consequential happens without rules you set or approvals you give.

2
Operative

Your team seat. Humans hold delegation, review and override; the org chart stays intact.

3
AI Operator

A bounded machine role with explicit permissions — it acts, never decides what it may act on.

4
Office / Scope

The durable boundary: permissions, lineage and evidence rules that survive staff and model changes.

5
Receipts

Evidence of what was sourced, decided, executed, verified, accepted — or left open. Exportable, always.

Hallucination control

Grounded answers, or an honest “I don't know”

  • Grounded answers only from your approved knowledge — no open improvisation.
  • Confidence gating: low-confidence moments are disclosed and escalated to a human.
  • Every factual claim carries a source receipt.
  • Forbidden-topic list per client, enforced at the substrate level.
  • Nightly regression tests on call flows — scripts drift, we catch it.

DOCTRINE

Governance compounds in the substrate — it accumulates as policy

Controls live inside the HazirMinds Operating Substrate: they apply to every agent, every workflow, every deployment — automatically, not by memo.

DOCTRINE

Office persists, agents execute

The Office (scope, permissions, lineage, evidence) outlives every individual agent. Change a model, swap a specialist — the office and its rules stay put.

DOCTRINE

Capability plateaus, governance compounds

Every vendor can rent the same models; capability converges. What compounds is the governed record of what your AI did, was allowed to do, and proved it did.
